Now when the Greeks heard that Diogenes had been captured,
they made Michael son of Constantine king over them.
And he seized his mother,
who was the wife of Diogenes,
and by force he settled her in a monastery.
And John, his uncle, became Caesar.
Now Diogenes, when he entered the land of the Romans
and heard what had happened,
went up to the fortress of Dokeia {OCR?},
and found in it two hundred thousand dinars,
and sent them to the Sultan with those two emirs who had gone with him,
and informed him of the matter.
And he put on the habit of the monastic life
and dwelt in Dokeia {OCR?}.
And he sent to Michael and said:
"Until now I have fought a good fight on behalf of the welfare of the Christians,
and it has been hard for me.
But you, blessed be your kingdom,
and you have done well in becoming king,
for it was your due.
But in good faith I counsel you not to break the peace which I made with the Sultan;
otherwise no rest will remain,
neither for you
nor for the Christians."
And Michael accepted his kindness and said:
"I will not depart from your counsel."
But after some days certain men worked upon him,
and he sent to Diogenes and said to him:
"If you are truly a monk,
why do you have a dwelling in a fortress? You ought to go down to one of the monasteries,
so that we may send guards into the fortress."
But Diogenes grew angry and said:
"Of the whole kingdom of the Romans not even one fortress is left to me."
And he arose, stripped off the monastic garments,
and took the horses of the merchants of Dokeia {OCR?} by way of a loan,
and gathered an army for himself.
And when the son of Sennacherib, patrician of Lesser Armenia, came to him,
he seized him and put out his eyes,
and took from him eighty centenaria of gold.
And he grew very strong and came to Melitene,
and sent to Sultan Alp Arslan
and asked him for help.
And the Sultan promised him
that he would come in person to help him wherever need called.
And after these things
Diogenes moved from Melitene to Cilicia.
And John came against him
and besieged him in the city of Adana.
And when he captured him,
he sent and informed Michael the king.
